results.title: Large language models as mental health resources: Patterns of use ...
results.content: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly accessible, there has been a rise of anecdotal evidence suggesting that users may be increasingly turning to LLMs for mental health support. This study was to assess the frequency, motivations, and perceived effectiveness of LLM use for mental health support or therapy-related goals among the U.S. residents with ongoing mental health conditions who have used LLMs in the past year. Survey responses suggest substantial adoption of LLMs for mental health purposes, with 48.7% of participants using them for psychological support within the past year. How frequently and effectively are individuals using artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for mental health support? AI chatbots show promise for mental health support, but caution is needed regarding their limitations and potential risks compared with human therapy. Future research should explore chatbot effectiveness across diverse populations and develop clear clinical guidelines for safe and beneficial AI use in mental health practice.

results.title: Evaluation of large language models on mental health - Frontiers
results.content: # Evaluation of large language models on mental health: from knowledge test to illness diagnosis. This study systematically evaluates 15 state-of-the-art LLMs, including DeepSeekR1/V3 (March 24, 2025), GPT-4.1 (April 15, 2025), Llama4 (April 5, 2025), and QwQ (March 6, 2025, developed by Alibaba), on two key tasks: mental health knowledge testing and mental illness diagnosis in the Chinese context. Additionally, most of the studies focused on a single aspect when assessing the applicability of LLMs in mental health, such as evaluating the model’s conversational abilities or text generation quality. This study systematically evaluates the performance of state-of-the-art LLMs, including DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4.1, and QwQ, across two critical tasks in the mental health domain: mental health knowledge assessment and mental illness diagnosis. Keywords: large language models, model evaluation, mental health, knowledge test, illness diagnosis. Citation: Xu Y, Fang Z, Lin W, Jiang Y, Jin W, Balaji P, Wang J and Xia T (2025) Evaluation of large language models on mental health: from knowledge test to illness diagnosis.
